pairs.question: Quin vos opici dicitis mihi, quare, quod hamaxan Graeci vocant, nos "septentriones" vocamus? Non enim satis est, quod septem stellas videmus, sed quid hoc totum, quod "septentriones" dicimus, significet, scire id prolixius volo.
pairs.answer: Sed ego quidem cum L. Aelio et M. Varrone sentio, qui "triones" rustico vocabulo boves appellatos scribunt quasi quosdam "terriones", hoc est arandae colendaeque terrae idoneos.
pairs.derivation: Direct-speech exchange aboard ship: Gellius asks the etymological question, a learned companion (quispiam) answers. Question: stripped the narration framing 'Hic ego ad nostros iuvenes convertor et' and the two inline speech tags 'inquam'/'inquam'; kept the speaker's words contiguous across those tags; normalized capitalization of 'Quin' and 'Non'. Answer: the reply opens with a reported view the speaker distances himself from ('vulgus grammaticorum "septentriones" a solo numero stellarum dictum putat... "Triones" enim per sese nihil significare aiunt...'); skipped that non-committal preamble and advanced the start to the speaker's own operative answer beginning 'Sed ego quidem cum L. Aelio et M. Varrone sentio', ending at the first full stop ('...idoneos.'), before he turns to elaborating on the figure of the constellation.
